articles.title: More Details Emerge on Exploited PaperCut Vulnerabilities
articles.executive_summary: PaperCut has released a second emergency patch for exploited vulnerabilities, allowing attackers to gain unauthorized access. The patch addresses CVE-2026-82078 and CVE-2026-81578, which were used in attacks.
articles.technical_breakdown: The vulnerabilities were exploited through a combination of social engineering and unpatched software, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code. The patch updates the software to prevent exploitation.
actionable_mitigations: Apply the latest emergency patch from PaperCut
Review and update firewall rules to block unauthorized access
Monitor logs for suspicious activity related to PaperCut software
articles.telegram_snippet: PaperCut releases second emergency patch for exploited vulnerabilities, addressing CVE-2026-82078 and CVE-2026-81578.

articles.title: TerminalFix Uses Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs to Deploy Reverse-Tunnel Backdoor
articles.threat_category: Ransomware | Data Breach | 0-Day & Exploit | Nation-State/APT | Cloud & Supply Chain | Vulnerability / Advisory
articles.executive_summary: TerminalFix campaigns trick users into running malicious commands in Windows Terminal or PowerShell, increasing the likelihood of successful exploitation. This technique allows attackers to deploy a reverse-tunnel backdoor, potentially leading to data theft or lateral movement.
articles.technical_breakdown: TerminalFix uses fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs to deceive users into running malicious commands, which then deploy a reverse-tunnel backdoor. The backdoor enables attackers to maintain persistent access to the compromised system.
actionable_mitigations: Ensure all Windows systems are running the latest version of Windows Terminal and PowerShell
Implement strict CAPTCHA validation and user verification processes
Monitor system logs for suspicious activity and implement detection and response measures
articles.telegram_snippet: TerminalFix campaigns trick users into running malicious commands in Windows Terminal or PowerShell, deploying a reverse-tunnel backdoor and increasing the risk of data theft or lateral movement.
